page.overview:
Who is Antonio?

Antonio was a male Chupacabra chained to Gellert Grindelwald's chair in his cell during his brief imprisonment at the Magical Congress of the United States of America in 1926-1927. Most notably, it participated in Gellert Grindelwald's escape.

Antonio was chained to guard the highly dangerous Dark wizard Gellert Grindelwald during his imprisonment in the prison of the Magical Congress of the United States of America, following his exposure and arrest in 1926. The baby Chupacabra was part of the high-security measures, along with a shield charm and other defenses. At one point, Antonio became attached to Grindelwald, essentially transferring his loyalty to him.

During the wizard's extradition to Europe in 1927, under escort by several Aurors and Rudolph Spielman — the International Confederation of Wizards's Head of Incarceration — Grindelwald switched places with MACUSA official Abernathy using Polyjuice Potion. After the high-security flying carriage set off from the Woolworth Building, Grindelwald Apparated onto the carriage, eliminated all the Aurors, and destroyed Rudolph Spielman's wand. Panicking, Spielman opened the box that had been handed to him, which supposedly contained Grindelwald's wand, only to have Antonio jump out from inside and sink his fangs deep into Spielman's neck.

Once Grindelwald clambered inside the carriage, he grabbed Antonio from Spielman and rubbed him affectionately. Suddenly, however, Grindelwald looked at Antonio with distaste, judged the Chupacabra to be "so needy", and threw him out the door of the carriage as it flew above the Hudson River. It is unknown whether Antonio survived the fall.
